exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 A Moral Dilemma
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Jane: Luke, listen to this story I read in a magazine. It's about a moral dilemma.
Luke: A moral dilemma? You mean a choice where every answer is hard?
Jane: Exactly. A girl was taking an important exam when the student beside her suddenly fainted.
Luke: Oh no. So did she keep writing, or did she stop to help?
Jane: She stopped at once and called for help, even though it cost her the exam.
Luke: That was brave. I'm not sure everyone would do the same.
Jane: I really admire her. She put a person's life above her own success.
Luke: You're right. Later that girl became a famous doctor, didn't she?
exercises.translation_cn: Jane 给 Luke 讲杂志上一个道德困境的故事:一个女孩考试时旁边的同学突然晕倒;她立刻停下呼救,即使因此考砸;Jane 很敬佩她把生命置于个人成功之上;Luke 说那女孩后来成了著名医生。

options: A story about a moral dilemma.
A story about a sports game.

questions.stem: What happened during the exam?
options: The student next to her fainted.

questions.stem: What did the girl decide to do?
options: She stopped to call for help.
She kept writing and ignored it.
She left the exam room angrily.

questions.stem: How does Jane feel about the girl?
options: She thinks the girl was foolish.
She admires what the girl did.
She does not care about the story.
She feels sorry for the teacher.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 The Power of Kindness
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: A small act of kindness can be more powerful than we think.
When you help a stranger, you may never see them again.
But that person often passes the kindness on to someone else.
In this way, one kind act can travel far and touch many lives.
So never believe that being kind is a waste of time.
exercises.translation_cn: 一个小小的善举可能比我们想象的更有力量;当你帮助一个陌生人,也许再也见不到他;但那个人往往会把善意传给别人;这样,一个善举能传得很远、温暖许多人;所以永远别觉得善良是浪费时间。

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Money is more useful than kindness.
A small act of kindness can be very powerful.

questions.stem: What may happen when you help a stranger?
options: You may never see them again.
They always pay you back in cash.

questions.stem: What does the helped person often do?
options: They pass the kindness on to someone else.

questions.stem: How far can one kind act travel?
options: Far enough to touch many lives.

questions.stem: What should we never believe, according to the speaker?
options: That being kind is a waste of time.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Helping a Classmate
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Tom: You look worried, Mary. What's wrong?
Mary: This morning our classmate Anna fainted in the playground.
Tom: Fainted? That's frightening. Was anyone with her?
Mary: Yes. I saw her falling, so I ran over and held her head.
Tom: Quick thinking. Did you know what to do?
Mary: A little. We learned first aid last term, so I called the school nurse at once.
Tom: You did the right thing. Is Anna all right now?
Mary: The nurse says she just needs rest. I'm so glad I didn't just stand there.
exercises.translation_cn: Tom 看出 Mary 心事重重;Mary 说早上同学 Anna 在操场晕倒;Mary 看见她倒下,跑过去扶住她的头;因为上学期学过急救,她立刻叫来校医;Anna 只需休息,Mary 庆幸自己没有袖手旁观。

questions.stem: Why is Mary worried?
What did Mary do when she saw Anna falling?
options: She ran over and held Anna's head.

questions.stem: How did Mary know what to do?
options: She read it online that morning.
She had learned first aid last term.

questions.stem: Who did Mary call for help?
How does Mary feel about her action?
options: Glad she did not just stand there.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Paying It Forward
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Welcome to our radio show about everyday heroes.
Today we talk about an idea called paying it forward.
It means that when someone helps you, you help another person in return.
You do not pay the kindness back; you pass it on.
We hope our listeners will try to pay it forward this week.
exercises.translation_cn: 欢迎收听关于日常英雄的广播节目;今天我们谈一个叫'付出善意'的理念;意思是当有人帮助你时,你转而去帮助另一个人;你不是把善意还回去,而是传下去;希望听众们本周都试着把善意传递下去。

questions.stem: What is the radio show about?
What idea does the show talk about today?
What does 'paying it forward' mean?
How do you treat the kindness you receive?
options: You pass it on to someone else.

questions.stem: What does the host hope listeners will do?
options: Try to pay it forward this week.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Virtues We Admire
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lily: Our teacher asked us to name the virtue we admire most. Which did you choose, Sam?
Sam: I chose honesty. I think telling the truth is the hardest and most important virtue.
Lily: That's a good one. I picked courage, like the courage to help when others just watch.
Sam: Courage matters too. Why do you admire it so much?
Lily: Because doing the right thing is often scary, and brave people do it anyway.
Sam: True. My grandfather always says that small brave acts shape who we are.
Lily: I agree. Maybe honesty and courage really go together.
Sam: They do. An honest person needs courage to speak the truth.
exercises.translation_cn: Lily 问 Sam 最敬佩哪种美德;Sam 选诚实,认为说真话最难也最重要;Lily 选勇气,比如在别人旁观时挺身相助的勇气;她说做对的事常令人害怕,而勇敢的人依然去做;Sam 的祖父说微小的勇敢之举塑造了我们;两人认为诚实与勇气其实相辅相成。

questions.stem: What did the teacher ask the students to do?
options: Draw a picture of a hero.
Name the virtue they admire most.

questions.stem: Which virtue did Sam choose?
Which virtue did Lily choose?
Why does Lily admire that virtue?
options: Because it is easy to have.
Because brave people do right even when it is scary.

questions.stem: What do Sam and Lily finally agree on?

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Counting Your Blessings
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Thankfulness is one of the simplest yet greatest virtues.
When you feel grateful, you stop comparing yourself with others.
An old saying tells of a man who had no shoes and complained.
Then he met someone who had no feet, and learned to be thankful.
Count your blessings each day, and you will always feel rich enough.
exercises.translation_cn: 感恩是最简单却最伟大的美德之一;当你心怀感激,就不再与他人攀比;一句古谚讲一个没有鞋而抱怨的人;后来他遇到一个没有脚的人,学会了感恩;每天数算所拥有的福气,你就会永远觉得足够富有。

questions.stem: How does the speaker describe thankfulness?
options: As a virtue only for the rich.
As one of the simplest yet greatest virtues.

questions.stem: What do you stop doing when you feel grateful?
What did the man in the saying complain about?
What changed the man's mind?
options: He met someone who had no feet.
He moved to a new town.
